subject: Post-demo: Quick SLO check + pilot options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Quick SLO check + pilot options

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and three small asks so we can scope a short pilot and get you numbers fast.

Recap (from demo):
- Your main goal: integrate an extractive Q&A endpoint into your support product for near‑real‑time answers.
- Rough traffic shape: spiky bursts around release windows, steady baseline through the day.
- Data residency: US-only for PII, otherwise flexible.

Short asks so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated:
1) Target P95 latency for answers (ms) and acceptable P99 tail (ms). If you have both cold-start and warmed figures, include both.
2) Expected sustained QPS and expected burst QPS (peak-minute). Useful to give a percentiles table if you have it.
3) Any hard procurement/timeline constraints (e.g., must be Dedicated for legal, or timeline < 3 weeks).

Suggested next steps from our side once you respond:
- We’ll run a cost/latency matrix and propose a two-week Hosted quickstart with pre-warming strategy.
- If you need strict isolation or predictable sustained throughput, we’ll scope Dedicated as the follow-on (timeline typically 4–6 weeks depending on capacity windows).

I attached a short perf matrix template (fastlane_perf_matrix.xlsx) and a 1‑page quickstart scope (redwood_quickstart_scope.pdf) to make the answers quick.

Thanks — if you prefer a 15‑minute follow-up instead of filling the matrix, happy to book.

—So
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Alice Gomez <alice@fastlane.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Quick SLO check + pilot options

Thanks Soojin — great session. Quick responses below, and I copied our infra lead if they need to chime in later.

Answers to your asks:
- Target P95 latency: 120 ms; acceptable P99: 500 ms (on 90% of queries we need <200ms). Cold-start tolerance: up to 800 ms for first request, but prefer warm responses.
- Sustained QPS: 200 QPS typical; burst (peak-minute): 1100 QPS during campaigns.
- Procurement/timeline: we prefer Hosted for speed, but if Dedicated gives us consistent tail latency guarantees we could consider it. Timeline: pilot should start within 2–3 weeks if possible.

Can Redwood give an estimated monthly cost range for both a Hosted quickstart (with pre‑warming) and a dedicated baseline that supports 1k burst? Also how long to provision Dedicated if we choose that route after pilot?

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll pass the perf matrix to infra and return it tomorrow.

—Alice
Alice Gomez
Head of Product, Fastlane.ai
alice@fastlane.ai | +1 (415) 222-3344
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Quick SLO check + pilot options

Soojin / Neha — internal note before we reply to Alice with firm numbers. Key considerations from runtime/ops:

- Traffic profile: 200 sustained / 1.1k peak-minute 
  - Hosted can handle this with continuous batching + prefix caching; main risk is burst-induced queueing at token level that can raise tail latency.
- Warm pool approach: we can provision a small reserved pool for Fastlane in Hosted that keeps model shards hot (pre-warm warm workers) and uses autoscaling for bursts. That reduces cold-starts to sub-150ms for text-short tasks.
- Dedicated baseline: to support 1k burst with tight tails we’d recommend a 2‑node dedicated pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) with concurrent worker tuning; typical lead time depends on capacity windows but often 3–5 weeks if we reserve now.
- Cost rough order: Hosted quickstart (pre‑warm + burst buffer) estimate: $6k–$12k/month depending on token volumes and caching efficiency. Dedicated baseline estimate (amortized) starting ~$18k–$28k/month (committed) — exact after we map token volumes.

Proposed response to customer: give them the two ranges above, propose a Hosted quickstart with a zero‑commit 2‑week pilot (we monitor tail latency and QPS), and a clear handoff plan to Dedicated if tail > 400ms P99 persistently during the pilot. Also include a provisioning SLA for Dedicated (3–5 weeks).

I can draft the numbers into a short one‑pager. Thoughts?

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Quick SLO check + pilot options

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick fallout. Based on your numbers we can do the following and keep the procurement/timeline tight: 

1) Proposed pilot (Hosted quickstart) — 2 weeks, zero commit
- Configuration: Hosted API with a small reserved warm pool + autoscaling burst buffer
- Objectives: demonstrate P95 < 120 ms and P99 < 500 ms for your typical workload; capture tail behavior during peak-minute 1.1k bursts
- Success criteria: P95 <= 150 ms and P99 <= 400 ms across >95% of requests in the pilot window (if we miss, we recommend Dedicated follow-on)
- Deliverables: pilot telemetry dashboard, cost report, and a short recommendations doc

2) Dedicated path (if required) — scope after pilot
- Recommend 2‑node dedicated pool for predictable tails; provisioning lead ~3–5 weeks after signed commitment

3) Cost ranges (rough):
- Hosted quickstart (includes pre-warm): $6k–$12k/month (dependent on token volumes)
- Dedicated baseline (committed): $18k–$28k/month (dependent on config & utilization)

If that sounds good I’ll send a one‑pager and a DocuSign PO to get the pilot scheduled. I’ve linked the HubSpot deal and DocuSign draft here for convenience: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/8791 and https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/FL-POC-8791

Next step options:
- You fill the attached perf matrix and we start in 48–72 hours, or
- We book a 15‑minute follow up tomorrow to walk the matrix together.

Thanks — looking forward.
—So
